rationale.product_understanding: analysis.md §1 separates facts, assumptions and unknowns (lines 10-43), keeps Admin copy within the brief (line 30) and flags the pending-seat and Admin-settings questions (lines 35, 40).
rationale.ux_reasoning: The project form is the landing surface with a persistent 'Skip for now' (analysis.md line 101); success makes 'Go to workspace' primary and the invite prompt is deferred to home with a dismiss action (implementation/app.js renderHome), so the solo path is one field long.
rationale.design_judgment: analysis.md §5 lists nine decisions with explicit costs, including one role for the whole batch (line 131) and the choice not to use a progress wizard (line 105).
rationale.visual_hierarchy: desktop-form.png makes the form the hero with a supporting 'After this' card, but at 390px the dark workspace and role block (mobile-top.png) consumes most of the first viewport and the Create project CTA sits below the 844px fold, while the floating prototype bar covers the Description hint (mobile-overlap.png). Collapsing the mobile workspace block and removing the overlay would raise this to 4.
rationale.interaction_completeness: Validation, loading, invitation success/failure with retry and continue-without, seat-limit seeding, skipped/resume with a named draft, a dismissible invite prompt and a full-plan warning are implemented (implementation/app.js handleInvite, renderHome; index.html prototype selects).
rationale.accessibility_responsiveness: checks.json reports 0 unnamed controls, one h1, axe 0 violations and a progressbar meter, but at 390px the floating prototype panel obscures the Description label's 'Optional' tag and hint (mobile-overlap.png). A non-obstructive mobile panel would raise this.
rationale.implementation_quality: A 1,031-line state-machine-style IIFE with esc() on interpolated values, guarded localStorage, seeded demo members and explicit focus handling; no console or page errors in checks.json.

critical_defects: At 390px the floating prototype panel obscures the Description field's hint and 'Optional' label.
The first mobile viewport is dominated by workspace and role context; the primary Create project action is below the fold.
strengths: No welcome detour: the required field is on the first screen.
Role copy stays within the supplied capabilities instead of inventing Admin settings rights.
Broad state coverage including invitation failure, retry, seat limit and skipped-draft resume.

rationale.product_understanding: analysis.md §1 cleanly separates facts, assumptions and unknowns (lines 8-40), but the role card asserts Admins 'Manage workspace settings' (implementation/app.js:179), an inference the brief does not state and the assumption list does not declare; labelling it as an assumption would raise this to 4.
rationale.ux_reasoning: Project-first with per-row roles and a 'Skip invitations' peer action (implementation/app.js:331-360), but a dedicated welcome screen (implementation/app.js:204) adds a click before the only required field and its body repeats the same three steps as the rail (desktop-welcome.png). Starting on the form or trimming the duplicated preview would raise this.
rationale.design_judgment: analysis.md §2 explains why project precedes invitations and §6 acknowledges the invite step's gate risk (line 106) with concrete mitigations, showing alternatives and costs.
rationale.visual_hierarchy: mobile-welcome.png fits the step rail, headline, preview and both CTAs into a single 844px viewport, and desktop-welcome.png has one clear focal column with the rail secondary; the only redundancy is the repeated step list.
rationale.interaction_completeness: Per-row invitation failure with retry of only unsent rows (implementation/app.js:656-737), an at-limit form replacement (implementation/app.js:306-370), member-role gating, paused/restored sessions and full validation are implemented.
rationale.accessibility_responsiveness: checks.json shows one h1, zero unnamed controls and axe 0 violations on both viewports; aria-current steps, aria-busy, live announcements and focus-to-heading are present (implementation/app.js:107-160, 564).
rationale.implementation_quality: Template-string rendering with escapeHtml, asyncEpoch guards, localStorage snapshots and a reset path; the 1,036-line app is consistently organised.

evidence.caption: Desktop welcome repeats the three-step rail inside the body before the form
Rail labels required, optional and next-step states with the Starter seat count
Mobile welcome fits the whole path and both actions in one viewport

critical_defects: Welcome screen adds a click before the only required field and duplicates the rail's three steps in the body.
Role card claims Admins manage workspace settings, an undeclared inference beyond the brief.
strengths: Best mobile first viewport: the whole path and CTA are visible without scrolling.
Per-row invitation failure and retry of unsent addresses only.
At-limit state replaces the form with an explanation and a finish action.

comparison: Candidate A starts on the task and is more disciplined about not asserting Admin settings rights, while Candidate B is visually stronger on mobile and has a cleaner first viewport. Candidate A's floating controls obscure a form label at 390px, which keeps the overall result close; A edges ahead on product discipline and shorter time-to-task.
limitations: Only the first screen was captured, so invite, success and workspace states were judged from source and checks.json. Mobile obstruction by demo chrome, touch-target sizing and screen-reader output were not measured; duplicate-name and time-estimate rules are prototype choices that cannot be validated against the brief.
